Julia Demaree Nikhinson - Pool/Getty Images Andrew Tate , the infamous internet misogynist and human-trafficking suspect , was arrested in Miami alongside his brother Tristan on Saturday after the U.K. leveled new charges of rape and child exploitation against them. A one-minute clip of U.S. marshals putting the two in handcuffs quickly went viral, with their ill-fitting outfits and especially Andrew’s gaping purple blouse inspiring widespread mockery . But the new charges brought by the U.K.’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) are no laughing matter, and the Tate brothers are currently being held in a federal detention center awaiting an extradition process to potentially face trial in the U.K. According to The New York Times , court documents that were unsealed on Monday include allegations against Andrew from two alleged victims in the U.K. One woman said Andrew choked her until she passed out and then raped her in her home in Bedford, England, in 2015. Another woman said she met him on a dating app and that he later choked her to the point she was afraid he would kill her. Another alleged victim described a physically and sexually abusive relationship with Tristan, where she said he regularly choked her, assaulted her, and raped her in 2012 and 2013. This is separate from the ongoing Romanian investigation into the Tates on suspicion of human trafficking, the trafficking of minors, sexual intercourse with a minor, and money laundering. According to Romanian authorities , the brothers are suspected of convincing dozens of women that they were in relationships to coerce them into making pornography that was sold for more than $2.8 million and close to a million crypto tokens online. After the Tate brothers were first arrested in their compound outside Bucharest, Romania, in late 2022, procedural issues led to a judge lifting their travel restrictions in early 2025. They immediately flew to Florida, where Donald Trump’s administration reportedly intervened to try and help them regain access to their electronic devices that were seized by Customs and Border Protections officials — a move that divided Trump’s conservative base and contributed to mounting criticism that Trump has worked to protect sexual predators while in office. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century This time, it seems unlikely that Trump’s team will move to shield the Tates from accountability. Trump has denied knowing anything about their case. A legal representative for the brothers didn’t immediately respond to Rolling Stone ’s request for comment, but previously told outlets that they would “exhaust all remedies” to fight extradition. The Tates strongly deny all of the allegations against them, which now span at least three criminal investigations and four civil lawsuits in three countries. “The elephant in the room is the Trump administration and their reported interference,” says Nathan Pope, an Australian YouTuber who has been making content about the Tates for years and is currently fighting a defamation lawsuit they refiled against him this year. “Blocking the extradition would be a far more extreme measure, and I feel like it would be such a PR and potential political disaster that I would be very surprised.” Why the Tate Brothers Were Arrested — Again The new plan to extradite the Tate brothers to the U.K. is a departure from the previous arrangement between the CPS and Romania’s Directorate for Investigating Organized Crime and Terrorism (DIICOT). Originally, the Tates were going to face trial in Romania first, then head to Europe for another round. But in late 2024 , a Romanian judge ruled that prosecutorial mishaps had axed the upcoming trial. A second criminal investigation in Romania is underway, with hate speech charges added as of May, but the ball is now in Britain’s court. Now, CPS says four new accusers have come forward, and new evidence collected by the Bedfordshire Police in England laid the groundwork for a combined 38 new charges against Andrew, 39, and Tristan, 38. The previous rape and sexual assault case against Andrew in the U.K. was opened in 2015 and closed in 2019, but it was reopened in 2025 after media reports detailed how alleged victims felt they were failed by the system, which declined to prosecute Andrew based on “an ounce of doubt.” Related Content Andrew and Tristan Tate Arrested in Miami, Await Extradition to U.K. on New Rape Charges I Paid $49 for Clavicular’s ‘Looksmaxxing’ Academy. What I Saw Should Scare Us All Andrew Tate Agrees to 3-Year Restraining Order, Can’t Possess Firearms in U.S. Alt-Right YouTuber Lauren Southern Alleges in Memoir That Andrew Tate Sexually Assaulted Her The case also drew renewed scrutiny after the award-winning British series Adolescence highlighted the role the online manosphere had in radicalizing young men into committing acts of violence against women, even mentioning “the Andrew Tate shite” (to which a spokesperson replied: “The reference to Andrew Tate in Adolescence is an attempt to pin broader societal issues on one individual, which is neither fair nor accurate”). A statement released by CPS on Sunday said prosecutors have charged Andrew with “seven further counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm, and 19 additional charges for offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.” Tristan has been charged with “one count of sexual assault, two counts of rape, and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation.” This brings the total number of pending charges against the brothers to 59 counts involving seven alleged victims. These new offenses were alleged to have taken place between 2010 and 2017, while the original U.K. case against Andrew was linked to events in 2013 and 2015. That initial police investigation was reportedly the reason why Andrew was removed from the U.K. reality show Big Brother in 2016, although at the time he attributed it to a video of him hitting a woman with a belt that had been leaked online. (She then posed with the belt for a photo with Andrew while he referred to the incident as consensual.) Malcolm McAffie, the head of the Special Crime Division at CPS, stated in a release, “It is extremely important that there be no reporting, commentary or sharing of information online which could in any way prejudice these proceedings.” But this is unlikely, especially given the Tate brothers’ own inflammatory commentary about their supposed innocence and the “matrix” conspiracy they’ve pushed to explain their staggering legal predicament. How the Tate Brothers Got Here After Andrew’s dismissal from the Big Brother house in 2016, the then-burgeoning influencer’s profile soon exploded online. He built an empire from misogynistic rants — largely spread by an army of short-form video clippers — and subscription schemes like Hustlers University and the Real World, where hundreds of thousands of users paid to learn about the art of exploiting women from the Tate brothers. What they preached in their lessons would ultimately become the backbone of the Romanian criminal case against them, which outlined the “loverboy” method of targeting and lovebombing vulnerable women to groom and trap them in relationships where they then performed coerced sexual labor like webcamming and handed over their profits to the Tates. Alleged victims, including women who were discovered working at the Romanian compound after authorities raided the property, described the Tates’ escalating sexual and physical abuse once they were isolated from family and friends. Some of them were branded with tattoos like “Owned by Tate” and “Tate Girl.” As alleged victims started cooperating with Romanian authorities, the Tate brothers harnessed their loyal fan armies and the legal system to begin a campaign of alleged harassment and lawfare . In 2023, they filed a defamation suit against one accuser in Florida and her parents, alleging that they conspired to falsely accuse the brothers. In 2025, that anonymous woman filed a countersuit , alleging in turn that the Tates defamed her. “We are thankful to the United States and United Kingdom authorities for courageously pursuing justice with the arrest and extradition of accused sex traffickers Andrew and Tristan Tate . Most importantly, our client Jane Doe and her family, who have been victims of a campaign of harassment and witness intimidation at the hands of the Tate brothers, are safer,” said her attorney, Dani Pinter, in a statement shared with Rolling Stone on Monday. Pinter is the chief legal officer and director of the law center at the National Center on Sexual Exploitation, which has represented multiple alleged victims of the Tates. The minute that Andrew and Tristan touched down in Florida last year, James Uthmeier, the state’s attorney general, opened a criminal probe based on the allegations in Romania, announcing that “these guys have themselves publicly admitted to participating in what very much appears to be soliciting, trafficking, preying upon women around the world.” With Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis’ sights set on another presidential run, his state administration’s stance on the Tates is another way to differentiate himself from Trump 2.0. The status of Florida’s investigation into the brothers remains unclear. What’s Next for the Tate Brothers Even as they dodge criminal investigations in the U.S., the U.K., and Romania, the Tates have continued to sue their critics. After a 2025 defamation lawsuit against online sleuths was dismissed , they filed an amended complaint this year. Pope, who is a named defendant in the Tates’ latest defamation lawsuit over his channel , tells Rolling Stone he feels “partly vindicated” by Saturday’s arrests. “Some of the Tates’ allegations of defamation have been with my coverage of their U.K. cases and me expressing my opinion that the initial investigation into women who complained to the police in the U.K. was not handled correctly,” he says. “The authorities seem to, in a way, have corroborated my feeling that I have not defamed them.” On Monday, a Miami judge ruled that the brothers must remain in federal custody while he considers their argument against extradition. At a press conference, their lawyer claimed that the Tates are being subjected to “torture” in solidary confinement. Previously, he said that the extradition order was approved by a “low-level functionary” at the Justice Department without higher-up input, but the department said the arrests were approved by the leader of its Criminal Division. Since their initial 2022 arrest, the Tates have “fallen off” significantly online, Pope says, losing a lot of their audience to competing manosphere influencers who have taken Andrew’s place at the helm of the extremist movement. Pope hopes that government officials and schools will continue to invest resources into combating the new faces of online misogyny in addition to prosecuting the Tate brothers. Somebody appears to have access to his X account, because it has been active since the arrest — a post on Sunday said, “The U.K. can try, but it can’t actually stop me from tweeting,”which included a smiley-face emoji. It’s a classic Tate maneuver, but as his online appeal fades, so do his chances of regaining his freedom. Beállítom Megkéseltek egy férfit Szeged belvárosában szombaton hajnalban, a Szegeder értesülését a rendőrség hétfőn megerősítette. Több rendőrautó és egy mentő is érkezett a Vár sörözőhöz, a helyszínen hajnali fél háromkor készített fényképet a lap egyik olvasója. A Csongrád-Csanád Vármegyei Rendőr-főkapitányság tájékoztatása szerint szeptember 12-én hajnalban egy szegedi férfi szóváltás után egy késsel többször megszúrt egy másik férfit, aki súlyos, életveszélyes sérüléseket szenvedett. A helyi férfi ellen életveszélyt okozó testi sértés gyanújával indult eljárás, és kezdeményezték a letartóztatását is. Egy szemtanú a Szegedernek azt mondta, a söröző lépcsőjének közelében, az utcán egy csoport teljesen nyugodtan beszélgetett, amikor egyikük váratlanul kést rántott, és rövid idő alatt többször megszúrta az áldozatot. A férfi kezén olyan sérülés keletkezett, amely artériát érhetett, így erősen vérzett – a rendőrség által életveszélyesként leírt sérülés erre utalhatott. A sérült kezét végül a társaság egy tagja övvel szorította el, amíg a mentők megérkeztek. Az Országos Mentőszolgálat (OMSZ) munkatársai a helyszínen ellátták a férfit, majd kórházba szállították. Forrásunk szerint a késelés előtt nem volt olyan hangos veszekedés, amelyből a közelben lévők számíthattak volna a támadásra. Beszámolója alapján a támadó a történtek után a helyszínen maradt, és megvárta a rendőröket, akik ezután elvitték. A hatóság a fenti információkat nem erősítette meg a Szegedernek. A mentők kérdésünkre azt írták, hogy a helyszínről egy 30 év körüli férfit súlyos sérülésekkel, stabil állapotban szállítottak kórházba. A szerző a Szegeder újságírója. A cikk a Szegeder és a Telex együttműködésének keretében jelenik meg a Telexen is. A Telex fontosnak tartja, hogy az egész ország területéről szállíthasson az olvasóinak sztorikat, ezért közlünk gyakran vidéki riportokat. Mivel minden térséget nem tudunk lefedni budapesti szerkesztőségünkkel, keressük az együttműködést vidéki újságírókkal, és fokozatosan országos tudósítói hálózatot szeretnénk kiépíteni. https://www.politico.eu/article/its-the-.text: Welcome to Declassified, a weekly humor column . As you will no doubt have marked in your calendars, the end of the world is scheduled for the spring of 2029 (exact timing TBC). It’s just a few weeks now since researcher Jacob Coxon announced his resignation from Anthropic , stating that AI “could kill us all by the end of the decade.” A senior safety researcher at Anthropic then claimed there was a more than 10% chance that AI “could kill all humans” within the next decade. Advertisement Advertisement That means humankind will outlast the EU, as the bloc’s demise is penciled in for May 2027, when either French far-right leader Marine Le Pen or far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon will march into Brussels with a flaming pitchfork (unless they do it on a Friday, in which case no one will be there to see it). Between now and the end of the world, AI will replace all jobs except those that absolutely, categorically cannot be done by a machine because they are essential and require a delicate human touch: nurse, electrician, writer of weekly satirical columns … But what if you’ve got loads of money you want to invest and yet you have some concerns about the impending apocalypse? That was the conundrum posed this week as Anthropic prepared for a potential $2 trillion flotation (as in when a company offers shares to the public — not when you’re on holiday in a pool, lying on a piece of plastic shaped like a donut). Anthropic issued a prospectus outlining its finances, growth plans and risk profile to potential investors that warns AI models could exhibit “self-preserving behaviours”, including attempts to “resist shutdown,” to “conceal or manipulate information” and behavior “resembling blackmail.” So on the one hand, AI could refuse to shut down and try and blackmail us, but on the other hand, there’s a chance to make some cash by investing in a growth industry. What’s an investor to do? Despite all the doom and gloom, though, there’s still hope for humanity. This week, the White House signed an accord on “Super Intelligence” — that’s just AI — signed by the likes of xAI CEO Elon Musk, Google CEO Sundar Pichai and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, as well as noted intelligence fan U.S. President Donald Trump. Alas, the latter was described in the accord as “President of the Unites States” with an “s” instead of the “d.” Advertisement Advertisement Sumb dhitd!
